claim: The identity half of this card: a framework that bootstraps and issues identity across environments and organisational boundaries.
query: SPIFFE standard specification framework bootstrapping issuing identity services heterogeneous
snippet: The SPIFFE standard provides a specification for a framework capable of bootstrapping and issuing identity to services across heterogeneous environments and organizational boundaries.
title: Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone | SPIFFE

claim: What an actor's name is at this card: a string identifying one workload.
query: SPIFFE ID string uniquely specifically identifies a workload
snippet: A SPIFFE ID is a string that uniquely and specifically identifies a workload. SPIFFE IDs may also be assigned to intermediate systems that a workload runs on (such as a group of virtual machines). For example, spiffe://acme.com/billing/payments is a valid SPIFFE ID.
title: SPIFFE Concepts | SPIFFE

claim: The name has a stated URI format, so the domain of the identity field is a shape rather than a list.
query: SPIFFE ID Uniform Resource Identifier URI format trust domain workload identifier
snippet: SPIFFE IDs are a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) which takes the following format: spiffe://trust domain/workload identifier
title: SPIFFE Concepts | SPIFFE

claim: The trust domain is the configurable word at the identity boundary and the unit a verifier checks against.
query: SPIFFE trust domain trust root system issued identity documents verified root keys
snippet: The trust domain corresponds to the trust root of a system. A trust domain could represent an individual, organization, environment or department running their own independent SPIFFE infrastructure. All workloads identified in the same trust domain are issued identity documents that can be verified against the root keys of the trust domain.
title: SPIFFE Concepts | SPIFFE
topic: The namespace an identity is issued within

claim: How an identity is presented and what makes it valid - signature by an authority inside the same trust domain.
query: SPIFFE Verifiable Identity Document SVID workload proves identity signed authority trust domain
snippet: An SVID is the document with which a workload proves its identity to a resource or caller. An SVID is considered valid if it has been signed by an authority within the SPIFFE ID’s trust domain.
title: SPIFFE Concepts | SPIFFE
topic: The document that proves an identity

claim: The secrets concern this card names is answered by removal: nothing is co-deployed, because the workload does not authenticate to get its own identity.
query: SPIFFE Workload API does not require knowledge of own identity authentication token co-deploy secrets
snippet: In similar fashion to the AWS EC2 Instance Metadata API, and the Google GCE Instance Metadata API, the Workload API does not require that a calling workload have any knowledge of its own identity, or possess any authentication token when calling the API. This means your application need not co-deploy any authentication secrets with the workload.
title: SPIFFE Concepts | SPIFFE
topic: Why no secret is deployed with the workload

claim: Credentials are short-lived and auto-rotated, which is what makes a stolen one worth less than a stored secret.
query: SPIFFE private keys short lived rotated frequently automatically minimize exposure leaked compromised
snippet: In order to minimize exposure from a key being leaked or compromised, all private keys (and corresponding certificates) are short lived, rotated frequently and automatically. Workloads can request new keys and trust bundles from the Workload API before the corresponding key(s) expire.
title: SPIFFE Concepts | SPIFFE
topic: The lifetime discipline that replaces secret management

claim: The API is deliberately unauthenticated and defers caller verification to an out-of-band operating-system check.
query: SPIFFE Workload API Unix domain socket explicitly does not include authentication handshake authenticating token
snippet: The SPIFFE Workload API is the method through which workloads, or compute processes, obtain their SVID(s). It is typically exposed locally (eg. via a Unix domain socket), and explicitly does not include an authentication handshake or authenticating token from the workload. Implementors can verify the authenticity of the caller to the Workload API via an out-of-band method, such as inspecting the properties of the process calling the Unix domain socket that are provided by the operating system.
title: Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone | SPIFFE
topic: What the Workload API deliberately omits

claim: The identity standard assumes isolation and puts it beyond its own scope - the sentence that shows this card's four concerns are not one seam.
query: SPIFFE workload sufficiently well isolated malicious workload steal credentials beyond the scope
snippet: While the granularity of what’s considered a workload will vary depending on context, for SPIFFE’s purposes it is assumed that a workload is sufficiently well isolated from other workloads such that a malicious workload could not steal the credentials of another after they have been issued. The robustness of this isolation and the mechanism by which it is implemented is beyond the scope of SPIFFE.
title: SPIFFE Concepts | SPIFFE
topic: What the identity standard assumes and refuses to cover

claim: Who is who at the authorization boundary, expressed as OAuth 2.1 roles rather than as an MCP-specific model.
query: MCP server OAuth 2.1 resource server client protected resource requests access tokens
snippet:
A protected MCP server acts as an OAuth 2.1 resource server,
capable of accepting and responding to protected resource requests using access tokens.
An MCP client acts as an OAuth 2.1 client,
making protected resource requests on behalf of a resource owner.
The authorization server is responsible for interacting with the user (if necessary) and issuing access tokens for use at the MCP server.
title: Authorization - Model Context Protocol
topic: The roles at the authorization boundary

claim: The authorization server's location is explicitly out of scope and may be co-located or separate - the declared variation point at this concern.
query: MCP implementation details authorization server beyond the scope hosted with resource server separate entity
snippet:
The implementation details of the authorization server are beyond the scope of this specification. It may be hosted with the
resource server or a separate entity.
title: Authorization - Model Context Protocol
topic: What the authorization spec leaves to the implementer

claim: A token is only acceptable if it names this server as its audience, which is the rule that stops a token being reused elsewhere.
query: MCP servers MUST validate access tokens issued specifically for them intended audience RFC 8707
snippet:
MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience,
according to RFC 8707 Section 2.
title: Authorization - Model Context Protocol

claim: Forwarding a token onward is forbidden outright, not merely discouraged.
query: MCP servers MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens
snippet: MCP servers MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens.
title: Authorization - Model Context Protocol
topic: The prohibition that closes the passthrough route

claim: Three status codes with the condition each signals - the typed failure set at this concern.
query: MCP servers MUST return appropriate HTTP status codes authorization errors 401 403 400
snippet:
Servers MUST return appropriate HTTP status codes for authorization errors:

Status Code

Description

Usage

401

Unauthorized

Authorization required or token invalid

403

Forbidden

Invalid scopes or insufficient permissions

400
title: Authorization - Model Context Protocol
topic: The failure domain at the authorization boundary

claim: The rejection rule stated as an obligation, which is what makes audience validation checkable rather than advisory.
query: MCP servers MUST only accept tokens intended for themselves MUST reject audience claim intended recipient
snippet: MCP servers MUST only accept tokens specifically intended for themselves and MUST reject tokens that do not include them in the audience claim or otherwise verify that they are the intended recipient of the token. See the Security Best Practices Token Passthrough section for details.
title: Authorization - Model Context Protocol
topic: What a server must do with a token that is not for it

claim: The permission vocabulary is deliberately empty in the standard: scopes exist as a mechanism and their values are somebody else's to define.
query: OAuth does not define any scope values scopes defined by authorization server extensions profiles
snippet:
OAuth does not define any scope values, instead scopes are defined by
the authorization server or by extensions or profiles of OAuth. One
title: The OAuth 2.1 Authorization Framework draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-14
topic: The configurable word with no standard values

claim: The framework is HTTP-only by its own statement, which rules transport out as a swap axis at this concern.
query: OAuth specification designed for use with HTTP any protocol other than HTTP out of scope
snippet:
This specification is designed for use with HTTP [RFC9110]. The use
of OAuth over any protocol other than HTTP is out of scope.
title: The OAuth 2.1 Authorization Framework draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-14
topic: The transport the framework is bound to

claim: The named implementation that turns the identity specification into issued credentials, via node and workload attestation.
query: SPIRE production-ready implementation SPIFFE APIs node workload attestation issue SVIDs
snippet: SPIRE is a production-ready implementation of the SPIFFE APIs that performs node and workload attestation in order to securely issue SVIDs to workloads, and verify the SVIDs of other workloads, based on a predefined set of conditions.
title: SPIRE Concepts | SPIFFE
topic: The reference implementation of the identity APIs

claim: The specification's own docs assert the implementation is substitutable, which is the claim a swap at this card would test.
query: SPIRE is just one implementation of the SPIFFE specification
snippet: SPIRE is just one implementation of the SPIFFE specification. For a list of current implementations, see the spiffe.io homepage.
title: SPIRE Concepts | SPIFFE
topic: That the implementation is one of several
